extracted.intended_audience: law students, legal researchers, and librarians (especially UT Austin patrons) looking for Texas regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Practical research guidance for locating Texas agency rulemaking materials in the Texas Register and the Texas Administrative Code (TAC), using citations, tables of contents, online sources, and commercial databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Register — scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Register is a weekly publication that serves as the journal of state agency rulemaking for Texas. It includes proposed, adopted, withdrawn and emergency rule actions, notices of state agency review of agency rules, governor's appointments, attorney general opinions, and miscellaneous documents such as requests for proposals. Final rules are codified into the Texas Administrative Code (TAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know that the Register records rulemaking activity (including proposals and adoptions) and that final rules ultimately appear in the TAC. The Register is maintained by the Texas Secretary of State and is available back to its first issue (Volume 1, No. 1, Jan. 6, 1976). Note publication frequency (weekly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching the Texas Register by citation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Texas Register citation contains: Volume, Source Abbreviation (Tex. Reg. for Texas Register), Page number, Date (month day, year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 29 Tex. Reg. 11027 (Nov. 26, 2004) — '29' is the volume number, 'Tex. Reg.' is the abbreviation, '11027' is the page number containing the regulation text, and the date indicates the issue publication date. Use these elements to locate the exact issue and page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching the Texas Register without a citation — Table of Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issue has a Table of Contents at the beginning organized by category of rulemaking action (Emergency Rules, Proposed Rules, Withdrawn Rules, Adopted Rules, etc.), with agencies arranged alphabetically within categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the short descriptive subject headings under each agency; these headings list citations to the relevant TAC section(s) and the page number where the document begins. If an agency has no items that week, it won't be listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching the Texas Register online (Secretary of State)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Secretary of State maintains the full text of the current issue of the Texas Register on its Web site in both HTML and PDF formats; previous issues are also available from the first issue to the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Secretary of State site to access current and historical issues in full text (HTML/PDF). This is the authoritative online source for the Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Westlaw coverage of the Texas Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Westlaw provides the full text of all documents published in the Texas Register from October 1989 through the present in its Texas Administrative Register database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Westlaw, look under U.S. State Materials > Texas > Administrative & Executive Materials for the Texas Administrative Register database to retrieve Register documents dating back to Oct 1989.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexis coverage of the Texas Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexis provides the full text of all documents published in the Texas Register from January 1, 1992 through the present in its Statutes & Regulations folder, States – Legal > Texas database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may need to click on 'More Sources' if the Texas Register database is not immediately listed in Lexis; coverage begins Jan. 1, 1992.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Administrative Code (TAC) — scope and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Administrative Code (TAC) is the official compilation of all state agency rules in Texas, created in 1977 by the Texas Legislature under the Administrative Code Act (Government Code, §§2002.051-2002.056). There are 16 titles in the TAC, each representing a subject category; regulations of each agency are assigned to the appropriate title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the TAC to find the codified, currently effective text of agency rules; know that titles correspond to subject areas and agencies' rules are organized under appropriate titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching the TAC by citation
rubrics_metrics.description: A TAC citation contains: Title, Source abbreviation (Tex. Admin. Code for the Texas Administrative Code), Section number, Date (year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 31 Tex. Admin. Code § 201.1 (2005) — '31' is the Title number, 'Tex. Admin. Code' is the abbreviation, '§ 201.1' is the section, and the year indicates the volume year in which the regulation is found. Use these elements to locate the section in print or online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching the TAC without a citation — General Index
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Index is a subject index arranged in alphabetical order, located in the last two volumes of the TAC. Under general subject headings and specific sub-headings, the General Index provides detailed cross-references to relevant rules and regulations adopted by the various agencies, commissions, and departments of the State of Texas and codified in the TAC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the General Index to find rules by topic when you don't have a citation; it points to the appropriate Title/Chapter/Section where a subject is regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching the TAC online (Secretary of State)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Secretary of State maintains the full text of the TAC on its website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TAC may be browsed online by Title, Part, Chapter, Subchapter and Section — use this navigation for targeted retrieval of codified rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Westlaw coverage of the TAC
rubrics_metrics.description: Westlaw provides the full text of the Texas Administrative Code and also has historical versions of the TAC dating back to 2002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Westlaw's Texas Administrative Code database under U.S. State Materials > Texas > Administrative & Executive Materials to access current and archival versions (historical coverage from 2002).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexis coverage of the TAC
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexis provides the full text of the TAC in its Statutes, Regulations, Administrative Materials & Court Rules folder, located in the States – Legal > Texas database, but Lexis only has the Administrative Code currently in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on Lexis for the currently effective TAC text; for historical versions, use other sources (e.g., Westlaw or Secretary of State archival materials).
